name: Tomnomnom
milestone_by_age_26: Tom Hudson (TomNomNom) is known for recon/tooling (e.g., gron, httprobe) and Detectify research; CSV birth ~1985. Tool popularity and public brand are mid/late-2010s; no verified material ≤26 milestone with two sources.
evidence_summary: TomNomNom is a respected open-source security tool author. Birth year and early career dates are thinly documented; defining public tooling fame is not tied to a clear age ≤26 dated milestone.

milestone_by_age_26: Australian security professional and Metasploit contributor (@TheColonial); CSV birth ~1985. No independently verified birth year or dated material ≤26 milestone found.
evidence_summary: OJ Reeves is known in offensive-security/Metasploit circles. Available speaker bios lack a clear age-26 milestone and strong birth-year sourcing.

name: H. D. Moore
milestone_by_age_26: Founded the Metasploit Project in summer 2003 at about age 22, creating an open-source penetration-testing framework that became the industry-standard exploit development and testing platform.
early_history_summary: Born 1981; first professional security role as a teenager developing tools for the U.S. Department of Defense (~age 17). Continued exploit research and in summer 2003 launched Metasploit as a public resource for exploit code research and development.
family_context_summary: Not documented in detail in reviewed sources; secondary profiles note a difficult childhood and early independence.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Metasploit, DoD teen work, exploit research, open source security, full disclosure
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and SecurityFocus interview place Metasploit founding in summer 2003 under birth year 1981 (~age 22). Dark Reading and other profiles document DoD-related work as a teenager. Later Rapid7 acquisition (2009) and runZero founding are post-26 career peaks built on that early framework.
starting_point: Born 1981; secondary profiles note Honolulu origin and a difficult childhood with early independence; family finances not well documented.
current_position: Co-founder and CTO of runZero; former Rapid7 chief research officer and Metasploit chief architect.

trajectory.event: Did DoD-linked security research/development work writing exploits and traffic-capture tooling as a teenager.
Founded the Metasploit Project as a public exploit research and penetration-testing framework.
Ran the Month of Browser Bugs full-disclosure campaign, driving browser patches and industry attention.
Metasploit was acquired by Rapid7; Moore became a senior security executive while remaining Metasploit architect.
Left Rapid7 after years as chief research officer / Metasploit chief architect.
Co-founded Rumble (later runZero) for network discovery and attack-surface management.
Company rebranded to runZero; continued as co-founder and CTO.

name: Mudge
milestone_by_age_26: Published the influential 'How to Write Buffer Overflows' paper (Oct 20, 1995) at age 24 and authored early L0pht security tools/advisories (including L0phtCrack lineage) that shaped full-disclosure exploit research.
early_history_summary: Born December 1, 1970; graduated Berklee College of Music while becoming a leading member of the L0pht hacker think tank. By the mid-1990s he published foundational buffer-overflow guidance, security advisories on Unix/auth systems, and password-cracking tooling that made advanced attack techniques widely teachable.
family_context_summary: Not documented in detail in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: L0pht, Cult of the Dead Cow, buffer overflows, L0phtCrack, full disclosure, Boston hacker scene
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and archived L0pht materials place 'How to Write Buffer Overflows' in 1995 (age 24 for Dec 1970 birth) and document L0phtCrack authorship plus numerous 1996–1997 advisories still within age 26. Peer network (L0pht/cDc) and Boston hacker geography were catalytic; family capital is not documented. Later Senate testimony (1998, age 27), @stake, DARPA, Google, Twitter security leadership, and return as DARPA CIO are post-26.
starting_point: Born December 1, 1970 in Alabama; later associated with the Boston L0pht scene; family class background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: DARPA Chief Information Officer (returned 2024); former Twitter head of security, Google ATAP, and L0pht/@stake leader.

trajectory.event: Published 'How to Write Buffer Overflows,' an early foundational full-disclosure paper on buffer-overflow exploitation.
Published L0phtCrack-related work exposing weaknesses in Microsoft password encryption and continued high-impact advisories.
Testified with L0pht members before the U.S. Senate on Internet security vulnerabilities.
L0pht became @stake; Mudge took research leadership roles including VP R&D / chief scientist.
Joined DARPA as a program manager directing cybersecurity research programs.
Hired as head of security at Twitter following a major account-hijacking incident.
Returned to DARPA as Chief Information Officer.

name: Katie Moussouris
milestone_by_age_26: Defining public milestones—Microsoft vulnerability research/bug bounty leadership, HackerOne chief policy officer (2014), Hack the Pentagon (2016), Luta Security founding—are after age 26 under Infosecurity Magazine age (~45 in 2020 ⇒ ~1975). Early MIT/Harvard sysadmin and @stake (2002, ~age 27) are strong early career but not a clear dated ≤26 material breakthrough.
family_context_summary: Born and raised in Boston; mother was a biochemist who encouraged science study; father was a Greek immigrant jeweler.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother (biochemist/scientist) encouraged science; father was a jeweler—not a cybersecurity domain apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Moussouris programmed as a child, worked as MIT/Harvard systems administrator, joined @stake in 2002, founded Symantec Vulnerability Research, then built Microsoft bug-bounty practice. Birth year is not on Wikipedia; a 2020 profile states age 45 (~1975). Fame peaks are 2010s policy/bounty work. Family: biochemist mother; Greek immigrant jeweler father (Luta bio).

name: Window Snyder
milestone_by_age_26: Joined elite consultancy @stake as roughly the 10th employee in the late 1990s / ~2000 (~age 24–25) and rose in security architecture before leaving in 2002 (~age 27), establishing herself among the first generation of specialist application-security leaders.
early_history_summary: Born 1975 (Honolulu listed in Wikipedia; New Jersey also cited); mother Kenyan-born Wayua Muasa. Attended Choate Rosemary Hall (class of 1993) and Boston College, immersed in the Boston 1990s hacker scene as 'Rosie the Riveter,' then joined @stake early and advanced into security architecture leadership.
family_context_summary: American father and Kenyan-born mother Wayua Muasa; attended elite prep school Choate Rosemary Hall.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a cybersecurity family apprenticeship in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: @stake early hire, Boston hacker scene, Choate, Microsoft SDL, Blue Hat, threat modeling
evidence_summary: Wikipedia documents birth year 1975, Choate 1993, early @stake employment as ~10th employee, departure 2002 as director of security architecture, then Microsoft SDL/threat modeling (book 2004), Mozilla, Apple, Fastly, Intel, Square, and Thistle Technologies. Age-26 eligibility rests on early @stake hire and architecture track before/around 2001 rather than later CSO titles.
starting_point: Born 1975 to an American father and Kenyan-born mother; attended Choate Rosemary Hall and Boston College; entered the Boston hacker community in the 1990s.
current_position: Founder of Thistle Technologies (secure device foundation); former CSO/security leader at Square, Intel, Fastly, Apple, Mozilla, and Microsoft.

trajectory.event: Established herself as an early @stake security architect in the premier late-1990s/early-2000s security consultancy.
Left @stake after rising to director of security architecture.
Co-authored Threat Modeling (Microsoft Press) and contributed to Microsoft SDL / Blue Hat bridging hackers and vendors.
Joined Mozilla to lead security strategy.
Joined Apple as product manager for privacy and security across products.
Named chief software security officer / platforms security leader at Intel.
Founded Thistle Technologies for secure foundations on devices.

name: Alex Stamos
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded iSEC Partners in 2004 at about age 25 with four colleagues, building an elite security consultancy later acquired by NCC Group.
early_history_summary: Born 1979; raised in Fair Oaks, California; Bella Vista High School (1997); UC Berkeley EECS (2001). Worked at Loudcloud/@stake, then co-founded iSEC Partners in 2004, becoming known for high-end software security research and expert-witness work.
family_context_summary: Greek-American; raised in Fair Oaks, California. Detailed family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: iSEC Partners, UC Berkeley EECS, @stake, Yahoo/Facebook CSO, Stanford Internet Observatory
evidence_summary: Wikipedia documents birth year 1979, Berkeley EECS 2001, and iSEC Partners co-founding in 2004 (~age 25). Later Yahoo/Facebook CSO roles, Stanford Internet Observatory, Krebs Stamos Group, SentinelOne, and Corridor CSO are post-26. Elite school plus complementary cofounders are the clearest early advantages.
starting_point: Born 1979; Greek-American upbringing in Fair Oaks, California; UC Berkeley EECS graduate (2001).
current_position: Chief security officer at Corridor (AI security startup); lecturer/affiliated with Stanford; former Facebook/Yahoo CSO and SentinelOne security executive.

trajectory.event: Graduated UC Berkeley with an EECS degree and entered industry security roles.
Co-founded iSEC Partners, an elite application-security consultancy.
iSEC Partners was acquired by NCC Group.
Became chief security officer at Yahoo.
Joined Facebook as chief security officer.
Directed the Stanford Internet Observatory after leaving Facebook.
Co-founded Krebs Stamos Group cybersecurity consultancy.
Became chief security officer at Corridor.

name: Tsutomu Shimomura
milestone_by_age_26: Became a research scientist in computational physics at UC San Diego and senior fellow at the San Diego Supercomputer Center in 1989 (~age 25) after Caltech study under Richard Feynman and staff physicist work at Los Alamos.
early_history_summary: Born October 23, 1964 in Nagoya, Japan; son of Nobel chemist Osamu Shimomura; raised in Princeton, NJ. Studied at Caltech under Feynman, worked as Los Alamos staff physicist, then joined UCSD/SDSC in 1989, later advising on cellular privacy/security and gaining fame for tracking Kevin Mitnick (1995).
family_context_summary: Son of Osamu Shimomura, 2008 Nobel Prize winner in Chemistry; grew up in Princeton, New Jersey after birth in Nagoya.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a world-class chemist (later Nobel laureate), providing an elite scientific household and proximity to research culture though not identical computer-security domain.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Nobel-scientist father, Caltech/Feynman, Los Alamos, UCSD Supercomputer Center, Mitnick case
evidence_summary: Wikipedia documents birth Oct 23, 1964, Caltech/Feynman training, Los Alamos staff physicist role, and 1989 UCSD/SDSC research scientist appointment at age 25. The Mitnick manhunt (1995, age 30) and Takedown book (1996) are later fame peaks. Strong inherited scientific platform: Nobel-chemist father, elite labs, and supercomputing facilities.
starting_point: Born 1964 in Nagoya to chemist Osamu Shimomura (later Nobel laureate); raised in Princeton, New Jersey; attended Princeton High School and Caltech.
current_position: Computer security expert and physicist; former CEO/CTO of Neofocal Systems (until 2016); known for the Mitnick investigation and Takedown.

trajectory.event: Joined UC San Diego as research scientist in computational physics and senior fellow at the San Diego Supercomputer Center.
Testified before Congress on cellular telephone privacy and security.
Helped the FBI track and arrest hacker Kevin Mitnick, becoming a public computer-security figure.
Co-authored Takedown with John Markoff about the Mitnick pursuit.
Led Neofocal Systems as CEO/CTO around a major funding round for smart LED technology.
Ended CEO/CTO tenure at Neofocal Systems.

name: Limor Fried
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Adafruit Industries in 2005 (~age 25 under CSV/timeline ~1980) from MIT after SB (2003) and MEng (2005), launching a defining open-source electronics kit company for hobbyists.
early_history_summary: MIT EECS SB 2003 and MEng 2005 with a critical-design thesis on personal-space defense tools. Founded Adafruit in 2005 (dorm/early post-MIT), later moving operations to New York; became a leading open-source hardware entrepreneur and EFF Pioneer Award winner (2009).
family_context_summary: Grew up in the Boston area (Allston/Cambridge/Brookline); father a professor at BU; mother taught piano (secondary interview).
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a university professor and mother a piano teacher—educated household but not an electronics business apprenticeship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT EECS, Adafruit, open-source hardware, maker movement, ladyada, Eyebeam
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and MIT News document MIT degrees (2003/2005) and Adafruit founding in 2005 from MIT. Exact birth year is not on Wikipedia (CSV ~1980; some secondary ages conflict), but founding at '25' appears in public remarks and fits a standard MIT timeline. Maker-movement wave, MIT labs, and online parts distribution were key accelerants. Later EFF Pioneer, Wired cover, Entrepreneur of the Year.
starting_point: Raised in the Boston area; father a BU professor and mother a piano teacher; trained as an MIT electrical engineer (SB 2003, MEng 2005).
current_position: Founder and engineer/owner of Adafruit Industries; leading open-source hardware entrepreneur (ladyada).

trajectory.event: Earned SB in electrical engineering and computer science from MIT.
Completed MEng at MIT and founded Adafruit Industries to sell open-source electronics kits and parts.
Received the EFF Pioneer Award for open-source hardware and software community leadership.
Adafruit reported multi-million-dollar kit/parts shipping scale; co-organized Open Kinect bounty.
Named among Fast Company's most influential women in technology and featured on Wired's cover.
Named Entrepreneur magazine Entrepreneur of the Year.
Recognized as a White House Champion of Change (Making).

name: Phillip Torrone
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Hackaday (first post Sept 5, 2004). Under CSV birth year 1977 that is ~age 27; major MAKE/Engadget/Adafruit operator milestones are also after age 26. No independently verified material ≤26 milestone found.
evidence_summary: Torrone founded Hackaday (2004), worked at MAKE/Engadget/Popular Science, and is managing director at Adafruit with Limor Fried. Birth year is CSV-estimated (~1977); Hackaday founding at ~27 is just outside the age-26 cutoff.
